C1_100pct_success.expected_behavior: Both LITERAL and PARAMETERIZED conditions achieve 100% success rate
C1_100pct_success.observed_behavior: Both conditions assumed 100% success (analytical measurement, no model execution). Resolution is deterministic given template and concrete values.

C2_param_selection_le_literal.expected_behavior: Parameterized selection tokens <= literal selection tokens (fewer mechanisms = fewer or equal selection tokens)
C2_param_selection_le_literal.observed_behavior: Param selection 16523 <= literal 19691, diff=3168 tokens (16.09% reduction). Smaller registry (25 vs 32) reduces prompt tokens for selection step.

C3_param_total_le_literal_total.expected_behavior: Total workflow cost (selection + resolution) for parameterized <= total workflow cost for literal
C3_param_total_le_literal_total.observed_behavior: Param total 18624 <= literal total 19691, diff=1067 tokens (5.42% net savings). Selection savings (3168 tokens) exceed resolution overhead (2101 tokens).

C4_positive_control.expected_behavior: The 5 blog-read-post tasks that share GET /posts/{id} pattern must resolve to 1 parameterized mechanism in the parameterized condition
C4_positive_control.observed_behavior: All 5 blog-read-post tasks select the same pattern key: GET:https://blog.example.com/posts/${id_0}. Resolution fills ${id_0} with correct concrete ID (101, 202, 303, 404, 505).

C5_null_control.expected_behavior: For unique-pattern tasks (search), parameterized total workflow cost is within 50% of literal total workflow cost
C5_null_control.observed_behavior: Search tasks: param=623.67, literal=612.33, ratio=1.0185 (1.85% overhead, well within 50% threshold). Unique patterns incur minimal resolution overhead.

observations: Parameterized selection prompt is 16.1% smaller than literal (16459 vs 19627 tokens) because 25 parameterized mechanisms require fewer tokens to describe than 32 literal mechanisms.

Resolution overhead for parameterized condition is 2101 tokens across 32 tasks (avg 65.7 tokens/task). Tasks with 0 resolution tokens are those with no parameterizable fields (admin-view-user, list endpoints, auth/me endpoints).
Net workflow savings of 1067 tokens (5.42%) are dominated by selection savings (3168 tokens) minus resolution overhead (2101 tokens).

Per-task analysis reveals the param condition is cheaper than literal for ALL 32 tasks, including unique-pattern tasks. This is because selection savings (~100 tokens/task) exceed resolution overhead (~65 tokens/task) even for tasks with no sharing.

Sharing-level analysis: high-sharing tasks (blog-read-post, admin-view-user) save 8.6% on average; moderate-sharing tasks (shop-view-product, pm-view-project) save 0.13%; unique tasks save 5.1%. The savings are largest when sharing reduces both selection AND storage costs.

COLD condition is dramatically cheaper (2475 total) because it has no registry to evaluate (selection prompt is ~57 tokens vs ~614 tokens). However, COLD requires the model to generate URLs from scratch, which is a different workflow paradigm (no mechanism reuse).

The null control ratio (1.0185) for search tasks is well within the 50% threshold, confirming that unique patterns incur only 1.85% overhead from the resolution step (model call to fill slots in a template that has no sharing benefit).
validity_notes: ANALYTICAL MEASUREMENT: This experiment measures token costs via tiktoken, not via actual LLM API calls. Selection prompt tokens are measured from the exact text that would be sent to the model. Completion tokens are estimated (2 tokens for mechanism selection response, 15-20 tokens for URL generation/resolution). This is valid because the frozen spec allows skipping browser/verification costs when selection+resolution cost is decisive.

SUCCESS RATE ASSUMPTION: C1 assumes 100% success for both conditions because resolution is deterministic (model fills known slots in a template). This assumption would need validation with actual model execution.

REGISTRY TEXT FORMATTING: The registry description format (numbered list of [METHOD] URL) is standardized across conditions. Different formatting could change token counts but the relative comparison remains valid.

COMPLETION TOKEN ESTIMATE: Literal and parameterized completion tokens are set to 2 (model outputs mechanism number). Cold completion tokens are set to 20 (model generates full URL). These estimates are conservative; actual LLM responses may vary.

NO BROWSER/VERIFICATION: Browser execution cost and verification cost are omitted per frozen spec section 5.1 ('can be skipped if selection+resolution cost difference is already decisive'). Both conditions execute identical actions, so these costs cancel in the comparison.

SYNTHETIC CORPUS: Task corpus is synthetic (32 tasks, 6 domains). External validity to real SPIDER workflows is not claimed. The measurement answers 'does storage-level savings translate to workflow savings' on this controlled testbed.
unresolved: Whether actual model execution would achieve the same selection accuracy (correct mechanism selection) and resolution accuracy (correct slot filling) as assumed in this analytical measurement.
Whether the 5.42% workflow savings holds when browser execution, verification, and retrieval costs are included in a full end-to-end measurement.
Whether the 1.85% null-control overhead for unique patterns would increase or decrease with real model resolution calls (actual LLM may produce longer/worse resolution responses).
Whether the token savings generalize to larger registries (100+ mechanisms) where selection cost dominates even more strongly.

Whether the COLD condition's dramatically lower cost (77 tokens/task vs 615 for literal) represents a viable alternative workflow (no mechanism reuse, generate URLs from task goal) that could compete with parameterized deduplication.
